text: Trestles down the whole wall, and cloth over every one
of them, hung to dry in the cold air off the pass.
The loom. It is bigger than the room and everybody
knows it. Getting it up here took four neighbours, a rope,
and a window that has never shut properly since.
Fleece in sacks to the rafters, and a smell of lanolin
you stop noticing about a minute after you stop
Finished bolts stacked to the rafters, sorted by dye lot.
You could clothe the whole of Kellowmere from this wall,
and one hard winter they very nearly did.
One shelf, apart from the others, holding the orange.
Nobody in Kellowmere will buy it and nobody in this
A pot of something spiky that has been carried up here
to be out of the way, and has decided it likes it.
It is taller than the loom now.
